chunks: your focus on the cultivation of the land be more profound than your focus on the collection of revenue,
for that [revenue] cannot be attained except through cultivation,
and whoever seeks revenue without [prior] cultivation ruins the lands,
and his rule will not remain steady for long.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between land cultivation and tax collection in Imam Ali's governance model?
ai.summary: This directive establishes the foundational Shia political principle of 'Iqan al-Dar' (consolidating the state through economic prosperity), prioritizing long-term stability over short-term fiscal extraction. It reflects the historical context of Egypt under Malik al-Ashtar, where efficient tax collection was contingent upon encouraging agricultural productivity, thereby linking administrative justice to divine order. The warning against 'Irbab' (ruin) underscores the theological view that unjust governance leads to societal decay, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the duties of the ruler.

en.sayed-ali-raza: You should also keep an eye on
the cultivation of the land more than on the collection of revenue
because revenue cannot be had without cultivation
and whoever asks for revenue without cultivation, ruins the area
and brings death to the people.
His rule will not last only a moment.
